question: How does Morgan Stanley convert workplace and stock-plan participants into wealth management clients?

claims.text: On the 4Q24 call (January 2025), CFO Sharon Yeshaya described "channel migration": Workplace assets that begin in Workplace and move into the advisor-led channel. She said that since 2020, $300 billion had come from Workplace and moved into advisor-led.

On the 4Q24 call (January 2025), Yeshaya said Morgan Stanley has an exclusive partnership with Carta, under which Carta will refer private companies and their stock plans to Morgan Stanley as they go public. She said the firm is committed to a seamless experience for those clients.

On the 1Q25 call (April 2025), Yeshaya cited an incremental $20 billion that quarter migrating to the advisor-led channel from workplace. She said this added to the roughly $300 billion accumulated from workplace since the channel was expanded in 2020.

On the 2Q25 call (July 2025), Yeshaya said 70% of the flows that originate from workplace are net new assets to the firm. She also said the firm used to say about $16 billion per year originated from workplace and was running ahead of that. She said advisor-led flows come from existing advisors, recruits and the origination of workplace.

On the 3Q25 call (October 2025), Yeshaya said the $300 billion workplace-migration figure had been accompanied by about $60 billion of migration per year. She said that three quarters into the year the firm was already exceeding that on a full-year basis. She also described LeadIQ, an AI-powered lead distribution platform that matches workplace and self-directed relationships with financial advisors.

On the 4Q25 call (January 2026), a company representative said advisor-led assets originating from workplace and E*TRADE relationships grew to a record $99 billion for the full year, compared with historical averages of around $60 billion per year. CEO Ted Pick said the three channels (financial advisors, Workplace, E*TRADE) together make up the firm's "strategic client acquisition model".

The January 2026 strategic update deck defines "Advisor-Led Flows from Workplace and E*TRADE" as assets brought into advisor-led relationships where the initial account was workplace or self-directed. The deck's figures are averaged over 2020 to 2024.

On the 1Q26 call (April 2026), Yeshaya said that since 2020 the firm had generated over $400 billion of new adviser-led assets from relationships that originated in Workplace or E*TRADE. She said that, including Workplace assets on the platform before the E*TRADE acquisition, adviser-led assets sourced from Workplace and E*TRADE exceed $1.2 trillion, roughly 20% of $5.8 trillion of adviser-led assets. She described a first step of retaining vested assets (greater retention that quarter, which translated into NNA), followed by channel migration as Workplace assets seek advice.

On the 2Q26 call (July 2026), Yeshaya said new accounts and existing clients both contribute, and it is hard to say exactly where each lands. She said that for those without an advice-based relationship, "we're working on that referral model". She said this can begin as early as financial education and can include 401(k) assets that are not IPO-specific. Pick said growth led by workplace relationships "reflects a cornerstone of our client acquisition funnel".

On the 3Q26 call (October 2026), Pick said the firm has an integrated funnel of self-directed, a "differentiated workplace offering that continues to expand and source new relationships", and the financial adviser relationship. Yeshaya said that as IPOs come to market, "real relationships, adviser-led relationships" are being built, and described this as the top part of the funnel.

The 10-K for 2025 (published February 2026) reports the workplace channel at December 31, 2025: stock plan unvested assets of $534 billion (versus $475 billion at the end of 2024) and 6.5 million participants (versus 6.6 million). The 10-K says the participant count declined slightly primarily because of the disposition of the EMEA stock plan business.

The 1Q26 10-Q (May 2026) reports stock plan unvested public assets of $475 billion and stock plan participants of 6.6 million at March 31, 2026 (December 31, 2025: $534 billion and 6.5 million). The 2Q26 10-Q (August 2026) reports $658 billion and 6.6 million at June 30, 2026. The 3Q26 supplement (October 2026) reports stock plan unvested public assets of $638 billion.
For scale at the start of the build-out, the 4Q20 supplement (January 2021) showed 4,885 thousand workplace participants and $435 billion of workplace unvested assets at December 31, 2020.

The 2Q26 10-Q (August 2026) says net new assets of $148 billion for the quarter included just over half in inflows related to IPOs of certain clients in the Workplace channel. On the 2Q26 call (July 2026), Yeshaya said stock plan IPO flows were just over half of NNA, and that this more than offset seasonal taxes.

The 3Q26 supplement (October 2026) shows total Wealth Management net new assets of $232.4 billion and fee-based asset flows of $80.5 billion. On the 3Q26 call (October 2026), Yeshaya said fee-based flows of $80 billion had nearly half coming from a corporate retirement mandate. She said the firm is expanding its retirement capabilities and deepening engagement with plan participants.

On the 3Q26 call (October 2026), Yeshaya said that since acquiring E*TRADE and expanding the workplace offering 6 years ago, the firm has added over $2 trillion of net new assets, and now has $8.4 trillion in client assets and nearly 21 million relationships. This figure is for the whole funnel, not workplace alone.

On the 3Q25 call (October 2025), Yeshaya said that as IPOs come to market, people bring their assets to Morgan Stanley. She said they drop into self-directed accounts but also move directly into advisor-led accounts, and that workplace is bringing in assets into NNA and directly into fee-based flows.

The January 2026 strategic update deck lays out offerings by client stage. For corporates, founders and employees it lists financial wellness and employee benefits, founders wealth strategies, private shares trading and lending, IPO execution and support services, full-service wealth advice and asset allocation, and family office, trust and estate solutions. Under "Access to Capital" it lists MS at Work cap table management, cash management solutions, private capital markets, tenders, financing and IPO, and MS at Work stock plan and 401k.

On the 2Q26 call (July 2026), Yeshaya said the referral model for participants without an advice relationship can begin at the financial education stage and with 401(k) assets. On the 3Q26 call (October 2026), she said that as fund lockups expire, assets are distributed to underlying investors into individual accounts, which is another place the funnel moves into an advice-based relationship.

On the 3Q25 call (October 2025), the CFO cited an expanded collaboration with Carta in private markets as part of investing in the platform. The 4Q24 call (January 2025) described Carta as referring private companies' stock plans to Morgan Stanley as they approach going public.

The 2025 10-K describes Wealth Management's offering as including workplace services such as stock plan administration, securities-based lending, residential and commercial real estate loans, banking, cash management and retirement plan services. On the 2Q25 call (July 2025), Yeshaya said household lending penetration grew across the advisor-led channel.

On the 2Q26 call (July 2026), a Wolfe Research analyst asked about press coverage of smaller RIAs using more aggressive pricing to compete for workplace business and about sustaining client conversion rates. Yeshaya replied that "it's always been a competitive business". She said the firm keeps adding capabilities, options and a greater lens of investment, and that it starts with corporate coverage, using the Integrated Firm to build corporate relationships at the top of the funnel.

The 2025 10-K (February 2026) says Morgan Stanley's ability to compete across channels (advisor led, workplace and digital direct) is affected by multiple factors. These include brand and reputation, the breadth, depth and pricing of product offerings, and technology supporting evolving client needs.

The 4Q24 call (January 2025) named headwinds for workplace: Yeshaya said the firm had not been in a cycle with many monetization events, and that participant counts were affected by sold stock plan businesses in Europe and Asia and by headcount reductions or acquisitions at plan companies. On the 1Q25 call (April 2025), she said workplace is "a little bit less in our control", citing stock grants and the possibility of fewer IPO events.

The 2Q26 10-Q (August 2026) says NNA is influenced by factors including capital market and corporate activities that affect assets in certain client channels, and large idiosyncratic inflows and outflows. It adds that "the growth rate of our NNA may be impacted" should these factors continue.

On the 4Q24 call (January 2025), Pick said the KPIs are whether the firm is increasing the TAM of relationships across the financial advisory lever, Workplace and self-directed, and fee-based flows. The January 2026 strategic update deck lists firmwide goals of a 30% WM pre-tax margin, client assets of $10 trillion+, ROTCE of 20% and an efficiency ratio of 70%.

On the 3Q26 call (October 2026), Pick said NNA "will ebb and flow in a given quarter". He said that, beyond IPO events, the firm's presence with many private companies leads it to believe "this cycle has many years to come". Yeshaya said she expects pretax margin to expand over time with scale, and that the firm intends to invest over the long term rather than manage the margin quarter by quarter.

adjacent.text: Trade press (InvestmentNews-type coverage, 14 October 2026) reports that more than half of the assets are tied to IPO-related flows, including the SpaceX IPO. It reports the CFO saying the firm should "continue to benefit" from the IPO market, and that workplace participants were up 2% and self-directed households up 5% year over year.
adjacent.differs_because: Trade-press reporting is indicative, not authoritative.

adjacent.text: Full-year 2025 Wealth Management net new assets were $356 billion and fee-based flows were $160 billion, per the 4Q25 call (January 2026).
adjacent.differs_because: These are total Wealth Management figures across all channels, not workplace-channel flows.

adjacent.text: A trade article (21 October 2026) reports a Morgan Stanley survey of plan sponsors. It says 69% rank their investment advisor or consultant as a top-three resource, and 45% cite helping employees understand their DC plan as a top concern. It also cites Cerulli (June 2025) finding that 63% of active 401(k) participants do not have a financial advisor.
adjacent.differs_because: Trade-press reporting is indicative, not authoritative. It covers retirement-plan sponsor survey findings, not Morgan Stanley's own conversion mechanics.

gaps.what: Morgan Stanley does not disclose a workplace-to-advisor conversion rate, or a specific cross-selling target or goal for converting stock-plan participants into wealth management clients. The firmwide goals cited are WM pre-tax margin, client assets, ROTCE and efficiency ratio.
gaps.suggested_source: Morgan Stanley investor day or strategic update materials, or an earnings-call Q&A on conversion metrics

gaps.what: A workplace-specific split of net new assets, and the number of stock-plan participants who became advisor-led clients, is not disclosed. Only the cumulative advisor-led flows originating from workplace and E*TRADE are given, and the 3Q26 stock plan participant count is not in the evidence provided.
gaps.suggested_source: Morgan Stanley quarterly earnings supplement or 3Q26 Form 10-Q workplace channel table, and investor day disclosures

gaps.what: Morgan Stanley does not describe the specifics of participant-level digital tools, financial wellness content or cash management and lending products used to convert stock-plan participants, beyond the offering lists and the LeadIQ and referral-model descriptions.
gaps.suggested_source: Morgan Stanley at Work product materials or investor presentations on the workplace channel
